options.text: percent-of-window only: admit when current weekly_all% + a small margin <= elapsed share of the week (the existing usage guardrail, unchanged)
options.say: percent-of-window only: admit when current weekly_all% + a small margin <= elapsed share of the week (the existing usage guardrail, unchanged)
caveats: ignores how expensive the NEXT spawn is - a 50 dollar Opus task and a 1 cent Haiku scan look identical until percent updates later, which lags real spend
options.caveat: ignores how expensive the NEXT spawn is - a 50 dollar Opus task and a 1 cent Haiku scan look identical until percent updates later, which lags real spend

options.text: dollar-pace: calibrate $/percent from usage.jsonl x post-analysis.json, convert each spawn's expected_cost_usd into an expected %, admit when projected % stays under the elapsed-share allowance
options.say: dollar-pace: calibrate $/percent from usage.jsonl x post-analysis.json, convert each spawn's expected_cost_usd into an expected %, admit when projected % stays under the elapsed-share allowance
caveats: the dollar-per-percent rate is noisy: only 1 of 3 detected windows had enough spend data to trust (124 dollars/point), and findings.md's reconcile gap is still open
options.caveat: the dollar-per-percent rate is noisy: only 1 of 3 detected windows had enough spend data to trust (124 dollars/point), and findings.md's reconcile gap is still open

decision.why: percent-of-window alone already runs as the usage guardrail and stays the PRIMARY live gate (it is what Servex actually tracks every few minutes); the small addition is converting each spawn's expected_cost_usd into an expected percent with the calibrated rate, so a decision log entry carries a real dollar figure and an expensive spawn cannot hide behind a percent number that has not caught up yet. Confidence held at 0.6, not higher, because the calibration itself rests on one trustworthy window (124 dollars/point) with real spread risk.
